standing.action: One scope decision covers all 37: whether these sites are in scope for consent tooling at all. Technical observation, not a legal conclusion.

standing.cause: No DMARC on the domain recipients actually see
standing.action: Nothing protects the brand domain from spoofing. Note this is a different question from whether the provider setup is complete.

standing.cause: From domain not aligned with sending domain
standing.action: DMARC fails on unaligned mail even when SPF and DKIM pass.

standing.cause: No SPF record on the sending domain
standing.action: Authoritative answer, genuinely absent. Mail from these domains cannot pass SPF.
All on plan(s) Sandbox. Sandbox plans get no automatic nightly backup, so decide whether these are production before treating as an incident.

standing.cause: PHP version past end of security support
standing.action: Receiving no security patches. Upgrade path is a Pantheon setting plus a compatibility check.

standing.cause: The consent sweep could not see the site
standing.action: NOT one decision. The 20 CM Pantheon sites here were measured on 2026-08-22: every one is a Cloudflare bot challenge on the client's own zone, reaching Pantheon not at all, across at least four DNS providers. The remaining 0 have NOT been attributed. All of them are UNMEASURED, not clean, and no consent rule scores on them.
A finding about the lookup, not the domain. Mostly self-inflicted resolver saturation; the next run usually resolves it.

standing.cause: WordPress core, plugin and theme status not observed
standing.action: API-only mode cannot see these. Any OK on these sites means clean-on-what-we-looked-at, not clean.

standing.cause: PHP 8.2 leaves security support in 126 days (2026-12-31)
standing.action: Fleet-wide deadline, not a per-site alert. Schedule the upgrade wave now; it is the only finding here with a fixed date.
Monitoring only. One policy decision covers all 49.

standing.cause: One pending Pantheon upstream commit, unmerged
standing.action: One merge decision covers all 32 sites.
416 update(s) across 27 site(s); the largest single backlog is hoffmanscheese at 27. Not one decision -- these are per-site and need scheduling.
